prompt:
You review one candidate interval in multichannel machine telemetry (entity machine-1-3).
The candidate is ticks [105,119) of the current 224-tick window (end excluded). A detector flagged it because of a sharp change.
Machines also make sharp changes routinely in normal operation, so a visible spike by itself is not an anomaly.
Picture: top heatmap = all channels over the window. Each row = one channel: left the full 224-tick trace, right a zoom (orange = zoom range, not the candidate). Black = observed, dashed blue = median of similar normal training windows; that median smooths routine spikes away, so a gap to it is not evidence by itself.
Decide the event validity of the candidate:
- "anomalous": what happens in the candidate is not something these channels do routinely: a new size, a new shape, a new combination of channels, or an abnormal state that starts or continues here. The candidate may be a small part of a longer abnormal episode; if so it is anomalous.
- "normal_repeat": the same kind of change recurs in these channels outside the candidate.
- "uncertain": only when the plots really do not let you tell. If the evidence leans one way, commit.
Detailed channels: [14, 11, 15, 12, 8, 29].
Return ONLY JSON:
{"event_validity":"anomalous"|"normal_repeat"|"uncertain","anomalous_channels":[subset of [14, 11, 15, 12, 8, 29], empty unless anomalous or uncertain],"channel_ranking":[ordered subset of [14, 11, 15, 12, 8, 29] that includes every anomalous channel],"confidence":"low"|"medium"|"high","additional_channels_to_review":[]}
